rows: Half a step is enough. You can call it nothing until it is your balance.
Brawling is measured in impacts. How many have you counted?
Danger is measured in consequences. Let me measure yours.
Pace is a measurable variable. I will keep it at the value I choose.
The people deserve a result they can measure. Give them the number.
The numbers are clear, and I will stand by them.
I earn my spot by what I do, not by what I say about it.
Measure the stance. The angles are set.
Technique, the measured one. Give me one measurable step in the hold.
Strikes have force and duration. Which force do you mean?
A gamble should be measured before it is taken. Did you measure yours?
A stall is a measurable loss of time. I do not give time away.
The people want a contest they can measure. Give them the numbers.
You call yourself among the best. Measure it. Give me one measurable result.
Measure your {strength} against the pride. Okay. Let me see what it measures against.
I have measured your {strength}, and it is narrower than your claim.
Cool head, that. Okay. Calm is a measurable thing.
That measures well. That is a precise point, and I accept the measurement.
I could raise my voice. It would not change the numbers.
One count, measured. Keep me down, and the measurement will be clear.
On the mat, every movement is measured. Stay in the measurement.
Grounded or standing, the measurement holds.
Stay in front of me and show me a measurable move.
A proper answer. The measurement is correct.
The measurement is still open. Give the measurement.
That I accept, to the decimal. We will measure it at the bell.
I will measure every step of this match, and I will finish it exactly.
My approach is exact. You will see the numbers on the night.
Whatever happens, the result will be measured.
There is more to come. The measurement is still open.
I have one more measurement to take, and you will see it when the bell rings.
I have no observation that establishes that claim. It fails my own test.
There is a difference between a measurement and an estimate. I have nothing reliable to support that accusation.
Agreed. Remove the unsupported claim. We can measure our wrestling against each other.
That correction is precise enough. The result at the bell is still open.
Watch the change in balance before each successful hold. That is an observable difference between us.
The result is measurable, and so is the work that produces it. We need not count anything we cannot observe.
An allegation is not a measurement. What observable result can this match provide?
What can we measure from the contest itself, rather than from the unsupported claim?
Your measurements of my {strength} give you a starting value. Allow for the angle I change when you engage.
You have accounted for my {strength}. Now measure how much time your proposed defence actually leaves you.
Correct. Without an observation, I have no measurement to record.
I'll accept that distinction. Let the result supply the data rather than our assumptions.
The years are one measurement. The balance of the next exchange is another.
Experience has value, but the result has yet to be recorded.
Experience lets me measure how much pressure a position will tolerate before I need to adjust.
A familiar angle still requires observation. I have learned to check the actual position, not assume it.
Your observations are from a previous contest. Measure the balance again when we establish contact.
You've studied the angles I used before. What will you do when the next angle is different?
I study the smallest shift in weight that changes the stability of a hold, then test it in training.
I prepare by measuring how far a position can change before the original response is no longer useful.
